newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS POISED TO TAKE CONTROL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS POISED TO TAKE CONTROL.

text.p: Juventus won 1-0 at Sampdoria on Sunday with a goal from defender Ciro Ferrara and now trail Italian league leaders Vicenza, held 1-1 by Internazionale, on goal difference alone.
Both Juve and Vicenza have 22 points, but the Turin side have played a game fewer and will move clear if they win at Udinese on Wednesday.
Vicenza, top for the first time in their 94-year history, took an 18th minute lead against Inter through Giampiero Maini.
But they squandered several easy chances to finish-off Roy Hodgson's side before conceding a 63rd minute penalty to French international Youri Djorkaeff.
Inter now lie third on 21 points. Napoli, 1-0 winners over Verona, and Bologna are a point adrift.
Bologna were stunned by an injury-time equaliser in their 1-1 home draw with Piacenza.
Arrigo Sacchi's first league match at the San Siro in five years finally ended AC Milan's eight-match run without a win.
Goals from Dejan Savicevic and Stefano Eranio secured a less than convincing 2-1 win over Udinese but the triumph was marred by the 86th minute dismissal of Alessandro Costacurta.
